harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Installed and configured httpd on node1 to serve an inventory application on TCP port 8181 while SELinux remained in Enforcing mode throughout. Added the 8181/tcp SELinux port label (http_port_t) via semanage, opened the firewall, verified the app responds correctly, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol with proof of changed boot identity and full post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1: RHEL 10.0, SELinux Enforcing (targeted policy), no existing inventory app, httpd/nginx not installed, firewalld active.
Installed httpd and policycoreutils-python-utils via dnf.
Created inventory app content at /var/www/inventory/index.html.
Configured /etc/httpd/conf.d/inventory.conf to Listen on 8181 and serve the inventory app via VirtualHost.
Added SELinux port context: semanage port -m -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181.
Ran restorecon on the content directory, confirmed SELinux still Enforcing.
Enabled and started httpd; verified it listens on 8181.
Opened firewalld port 8181/tcp permanently and reloaded.
Verified HTTP response from the inventory app over NODE_IP:8181 and confirmed no AVC denials.
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, SELinux mode, httpd status, port, app content).
Triggered a deferred self-reboot via systemd-run so acknowledgement returned before disconnection.
Polled node1 until it reconnected; confirmed boot_id changed from 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146 to 86692ec5-2a0d-46a8-8841-d538dc542eeb (new uptime 08:25:15), proving an actual restart.
Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux Enforcing, httpd active with new PIDs, port 8181 listening, firewall rule persisted, app content correct, no AVC denials.

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP port 8181 with SELinux enforcing (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed SELinux Enforcing and no web server; httpd was installed, configured to Listen on 8181, given the http_port_t SELinux port label, started, firewall-opened, and verified serving the inventory page content with no AVC denials, all while getenforce reported Enforcing.
Captured boot_id (7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146), uptime, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, port 8181 listening, and correct app content before the restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled a deferred reboot and returned its acknowledgement (timer/service unit names) before the connection dropped.
Poll attempts timed out and then saw connection reset, consistent with the node rebooting.

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id (86692ec5-2a0d-46a8-8841-d538dc542eeb) and new uptime (08:25:15), differing from the pre-restart baseline, proving the node actually rebooted rather than just becoming reachable again.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data and continued SELinux enforcement
evidence.summary: After the restart, SELinux is still Enforcing, httpd is active with fresh PIDs, port 8181 is listening, the firewall rule persisted, the inventory app returns correct content, and no AVC denials were found.
